# Tobit Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** As they went on their way, the dog ran along with them, and they spent the first night camped at the river Tigris.

**2** When the young man went down to the river to wash his feet, a large fish leaped from the water and tried to swallow his foot. He cried out in alarm.

**3** The angel said to him, "Grab hold of the fish!" The young man seized it and hauled it up onto the bank.

**4** The angel said to him, "Cut open the fish and take out its heart, liver, and gall, and keep these with you carefully."

**5** The young man did as the angel had commanded him. He cut open the fish, removed the heart, liver, and gall, and set them aside. He roasted some of the fish and ate it; the rest he salted and kept for the journey.

Then the two of them traveled on together until they were approaching Media.

**6** The young man questioned the angel: "Brother Azariah, what is the heart and the liver and the gall of the fish good for? What is the healing use of these things?"

**7** He said, "As for the heart and liver — if any person is afflicted by a demon or an evil spirit, one must make a smoke from these before that person, and he will be freed from all torment forever.

**8** As for the gall — smear it on the eyes of a man who has white films over his eyes, and he will be healed."

**9** When they were drawing near to Media and already approaching Ecbatana,

**10** Raphael said to the young man Tobias, "Brother Tobias." He said, "Here I am." Raphael said, "Tonight we must lodge with Raguel, who is a kinsman of yours. He has a daughter named Sarah.

**11** He has no other son or daughter except Sarah alone, and you are his nearest heir — everything he has will come to you. The girl is sensible, courageous, and very beautiful, and her father is a good man.

**12** You have the right to take her as your wife. So listen to me, brother, and I will speak to her father tonight about the girl, so that she may be given to you as your bride. And when we return from Rages we will hold the wedding. For I know that Raguel cannot refuse her to you or give her to another man — that would bring death upon him according to the ordinance in the book of Moses, seeing that you know you are her rightful heir. So listen, brother, and tonight we will speak to her father about the girl and ask her hand for you."

**13** Tobias answered Raphael: "Brother Azariah, I have already heard that this girl has been given to seven men, and every one of them died in the bridal chamber on the night he went in to her. And I heard that a demon kills them.

**14** Now I fear — because the demon does nothing to her but kills every man who tries to approach her. I am my father's only child. If I die, I will bring my father and mother down in grief to their grave, and they have no other son to bury them."

**15** The angel said to him, "Have you forgotten your father's command to take a wife from your own kindred? Now hear me, brother, and give this demon no thought. Take her.

**16** I know that this very night she will be given to you as your wife.

**17** When you enter the bridal chamber, take the heart and liver from the fish and place them on the smoldering incense coals. The smoke will spread,

**18** and the demon will smell it and flee and never return again. And before you come together with her, both of you rise and pray; petition the Lord of heaven for mercy and protection to come upon you. Do not be afraid, for she was appointed for you before the ages; you will deliver her, and she will go with you. And I think you will have children by her. Do not be troubled."

When Tobias heard the words of Raphael — and that Sarah was his kinswoman, from his father's own house — he loved her deeply, and his heart clung to her.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **v. 4**: "gall" for *cholē* (χολή) — the bile or gall bladder contents. This is the medically active substance in the fish used to treat Tobit's blindness (ch. 11). LOGOS uses "gall" as the formal anatomical equivalent in biblical English.
- **v. 7**: "make a smoke" — the Greek *thymiasai* refers to fumigation via burning. This is medicinal/ritual smoke, not a burnt offering in the temple sense. Rendered as "make a smoke from these" rather than "offer incense."
- **v. 8**: "white films" — Greek *leukōmata* (λευκώματα), the white deposits that formed over Tobit's eyes after the sparrow droppings incident (ch. 2). Medically this resembles cataracts or corneal scarring.
- **v. 12**: "ordinance in the book of Moses" — reference to levirate inheritance law (Numbers 27, 36). Raguel cannot legally betroth Sarah to a non-kinsman while Tobias lives. The word *krima* (ordinance/decree) is rendered formally.
- **v. 14**: "bring my father and mother down in grief to their grave" — a Hebraic idiom echoing Genesis 37:35 and 42:38. LOGOS preserves it without paraphrase.
- **v. 18**: "appointed for you before the ages" — *ap' aiōnos* (from eternity). This is Raphael's announcement of divine providence governing the match. LOGOS renders "before the ages" to preserve the temporal scope.
- Final verse: "his heart clung to her" — Greek *prosekollān*, consciously echoing LXX Genesis 2:24 (a man shall *proskollēthēsetai* to his wife). The allusion is deliberate and deeply significant. — LOGOS
